| Telescope | Optical background | Pulses / PMT | Muon-dominated samples |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| IceCube | PMT + glass noise | $0.56\,\mathrm{kHz}$ · 10-inch | $2.7\,\mathrm{kHz}$ · IC86 DAQ |
| KM3NeT | $^{40}\mathrm K$ + bioluminescence | $\sim7\,\mathrm{kHz}$ · 3-inch | $\sim1\,\mathrm{Hz}$ · ARCA6 reconstructed |
| Baikal-GVD | Water luminescence | $20–100\,\mathrm{kHz}$ · 10-inch | $\sim3\,\mathrm{Hz/cluster}$ · reconstructed |

### Neutrino backgrounds

![](media/backgrounds/neutrino_interaction_rates.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 540px;" fig-alt="Calculated neutrino-nucleon interactions per year per energy decade in one cubic kilometre of water from the downward hemisphere, before event selection. Conventional atmospheric neutrinos fall more steeply than the astrophysical component. A dashed prompt-charm prediction has a shaded theoretical band. Astrophysical best-fit extrapolations outside the sensitive range are dotted."}

::: {.media-caption}
$1\,\mathrm{km^3}$ water · downward $2\pi$ · all flavours, $\nu+\bar\nu$ · CC+NC · before selection.
:::

::::::

::: {.notes}
Spend about two minutes here. First distinguish one PMT pulse, a detector
trigger, and an event surviving reconstruction cuts. Read the last column
with its sample labels; the three rates are not equal-volume comparisons.
Earth opacity has already been discussed.

Optical singles are pulses per PMT, not event rates. IceCube's 560 Hz is the
average total in-ice rate for standard DOMs, not the 780 Hz HQE DOM rate or a
deadtime-suppressed supernova scaler rate; threshold about 0.25 p.e. Most
background hits originate in PMT/glass effects, including radioactive decays
and luminescence. KM3NeT's observed baseline is about 7 kHz per 3-inch PMT,
at about 0.3 p.e.; seawater K-40 and variable bioluminescence contribute.
Baikal's 20–100 kHz per 10-inch PMT varies with depth and season. Freshwater
luminescence must not be described as the same seawater K-40 background.

Atmospheric muons and muon bundles are the dominant event background before
neutrino-quality selection. IC86's 2.7 kHz is the median total DAQ event rate,
dominated by atmospheric muons, not a pure muon rate. Seasonal range 2.5–2.9 kHz.
ARCA6 denotes six detection units, not the full future ARCA. Its approximately
1 Hz is derived from 130000 reconstructed muon-bundle events in 1.5 days,
after n_hits > 50 and Lambda > 20. GVD's approximately 3 Hz per cluster is a
reconstructed, muon-dominated track rate in the 2019–2023 analysis. These are
illustrative observed sample rates, not comparable trigger efficiencies.
Downgoing muons can be misreconstructed as upgoing tracks or mimic starting
events through stochastic losses. Direction, fit-quality and veto cuts suppress
them; the plotted neutrino rates apply none of these cuts or self-vetoes.

The graph counts neutrino-nucleon DIS interactions inside a fixed water volume,
not detected or selected events and not through-going muons produced outside it:

$$
\frac{dN}{d\log_{10}E_\nu}
=\ln(10)\,E_\nu T N_A\rho V\sum_\alpha\int_{2\pi}d\Omega
\left[\Phi_{\nu_\alpha}\sigma_\nu^{\rm CC+NC}
+\Phi_{\bar\nu_\alpha}\sigma_{\bar\nu}^{\rm CC+NC}\right].
$$

True neutrino energy, not deposited or muon energy. All flavours and both signs
are summed. Density 1 g/cm3, volume 1e15 cm3, exposure one Julian year.
Downward hemisphere avoids Earth propagation; overburden attenuation is neglected.
CSMS Tables 1–2 give separate isoscalar-nucleon CC+NC cross sections. Using
isoscalar values for water is an approximation; tau-mass corrections and
neutrino-electron interactions (including Glashow resonance) are not included.

Conventional flux: MCEq H3a/SIBYLL 2.3c splines distributed in IceCube nuflux
2.0.7. Prompt: BERSS/H3p central/lower/upper predictions (electron and muon
flavours, each sign); shading is the supplied QCD model envelope, not a measured
confidence interval or a detection of prompt neutrinos. Prompt H3p assumes a
proton-only extragalactic CR component, unlike conventional H3a. These are
explicit benchmark models, not components of one fitted likelihood model.

Astrophysical flux: IceCube MESE broken-power-law central fit, PRD 113 (2026)
062002, Table 3: per-flavour nu+antinu normalization 2.28e-18 GeV^-1 cm^-2
s^-1 sr^-1 at 100 TeV, gamma_low=1.72, gamma_high=2.839, log10(E_break/GeV)=4.524.
Assume equal e:mu:tau flux and equal nu/antinu splitting. Dotted extensions
below 6.1 TeV and above 7.5 PeV are extrapolations, not measured flux bins.
No uncorrelated parameter-error band is substituted for a joint confidence region.

Optical noise sources:
[IceCube instrumentation, sections 3.8 and 6.1](https://arxiv.org/html/1612.05093v3);
[KM3NeT first-DU performance](https://doi.org/10.1140/epjc/s10052-020-7629-z);
[Baikal-GVD optical noise](https://pos.sissa.it/364/050/pdf).
Muon samples:
[KM3NeT measured muons](https://doi.org/10.1140/epjc/s10052-024-13018-8);
[Baikal-GVD track analysis](https://pos.sissa.it/501/1162/pdf).
Graph inputs:
[nuflux](https://github.com/icecube/nuflux);
[MCEq](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.00544);
[BERSS](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.01076);
[CSMS](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.3723);
[IceCube spectral fit](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22234#S4.T3).
Reproducible generator and checks: assets/backgrounds/README.md.
:::
